messages.subject: Bias toward 5' first bases ?
parts:
Hello everyone,

I used methylkit to extract the percent of methylation per base per samples (min cov 10X in all samples) from a RRBS experiment (MspI enzyme). We used a random forest approach to extract bases with significant methylation differences. 

We ended with ~324 bases CpG significantly differentiating our groups. Out of those, 48 bases are in position 1 of our reads.

Just wondering in the first 5' bases should be ignored since they depend the enzyme cut site (CCG/TGG) or if this is actually a biological signal ?

Best,

Jérémy

messages.subject: Re: Bias toward 5' first bases ?
parts:
Thank you.

I did see this post but it remains quite unclear 

1) How does 3' end-repair can ignore the first 5' bases ?

1) If the methylation % difference was only due to the cutting site (CGG or TGG) this wouldn't have been ignored with methylkit ? For instance I fixed a threshold with Methylkit a CpG with at least 10X coverage in 100% of the samples. If the cutting site is a TGG, the cytosine base will be considered as missing in this individual ? Most likely, the specific base will be ignored in downstream analysis ? I am right here ?

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: Bias toward 5' first bases ?
parts:
I think you should carry on if you make sure the bias in the first base is not due to wrong trimming and your library is directional. I don't know if you would get 5' end end-repair bias with non-directional libraries.

Best
Altuna
